title: Custody models, rotation sampling, and SIEM enrichment - proposal
content:
Purpose and audience:

This is a working proposal for how Redwood should: (1) map custody models for customer keys (BYOK/HSM/shared) into RBAC-v2 operations, (2) implement a lightweight rotation sampling strategy to meet existing rotation SLAs without massive throughput impact, and (3) enrich SIEM/log exports with denormalized key lifecycle evidence for automated attestation. Audience: security, compliance, keying ops, SRE, and product owners for Private/Dedicated.

High-level goals (non-normative):
- Ensure audit evidence is sufficient for SOC2/ISO-style attestations without requiring full per-request key material logging.
- Allow flexible custody (customer-owned BYOK, Redwood-managed, hybrid escrow) while keeping clear operation boundaries enforced by RBAC v2.
- Keep rotation CPU/GPU and HSM cost predictable by sampling operations and storing canonical evidence artifacts for every rotation event.

Section A — Custody models and RBAC mappings (sketch)

Custody model variants (we use shorthand):
- Customer BYOK (tenant-supplied keys in customer KMS/HSM): Redwood never holds plaintext keys; we store key references and metadata.
- Redwood-Manged KMS: Redwood issues and rotates keys; HSM-backed when requested.
- Shared-escrow: Customer keys are escrowed in secure vault (encrypted with an escrow keystore) for recovery; Redwood has constrained access paths.

RBAC v2 operation primitives to define (examples):
- kms.key.create (create key material metadata / request wrapped CEK)
- kms.key.rotate.init (begin rotation workflow — can be nonce-based or HSM rewrap)
- kms.key.rotate.commit (mark new version active for traffic)
- kms.key.rewrap (re-encrypt CEK under new master)
- kms.key.export-request (export wrapped key artifact to escrow system)
- kms.key.access.audit (read of key metadata; allowed but must be logged)

Mapping rules (policy notes):
- For BYOK, kms.key.rotate.* must be allowed only for actors with tenant-scoped RBAC grants AND require approval step for outbound operations (export/escrow).
- For Redwood-managed, internal role redwood:kms-operator can initiate rotations; rotations for production tenant keys also require 2nd-party approver (can be automation bot + shift lead).
- Escrow operations must be gated by time-bound approvals and logged as high-fidelity evidence artifacts (see Section C).

Unresolved/decision-needed:
- Do we require multi-sig/HSM-signed approval for every production rotation or only for escrow exports? (tradeoffs: operational velocity vs compliance defensibility)

Section B — Rotation sampling strategy (practical operational pattern)

Motivation: rotating every CEK on exact schedule causes high churn (cache invalidations, rewrap loads, HSM ops). Instead, rotate using proactively scheduled cohort sampling with coverage guarantees.

Key concepts:
- Rotation SLO: X% of keys rotated within SLA window (e.g., 99% within 30 days).
- Cohorts: keys assigned to deterministic cohorts (hash(key_id) % N) to spread rotation load.
- Sampling policy: each maintenance window pick M cohorts to rotate fully; remaining cohorts rotated opportunistically on first write or when touched by a qualifying event.

Concrete example (proposal):
- SLA: 99% of customer CEKs rotated every 90 days; 100% rotated within 120 days.
- N = 90 cohorts (one per day for a 90-day cycle). Each night we schedule rotation for 1 cohort + 25% burst capacity for on-demand rotations.
- On-rotate workflow: call HSM rewrap or customer-KMS re-encryption; write rotation-event artifact to evidence-store (see Section C); emit audit events.

Advantages:
- Smooths HSM/API load over time; predictable billing/throughput.
- Provides measurable coverage metrics (cohort-level).

Edge cases and mitigation:
- Cold objects (keys for rarely-accessed tenants): ensure forced rotate at 120-day hard deadline; implement a background sweep job to pick stale cohorts.
- Failures mid-rotation: use two-phase commit (init -> rewrap -> commit) and automatic rollback TTL; if commit not observed within TTL, mark rotation-incomplete and requeue.

Section C — Evidence artifact model and SIEM enrichment schema

Problem statement: SIEM and compliance need deterministic evidence that rotation occurred and who authorized it. Raw audit logs alone are noisy and sometimes insufficient for attestations (e.g., need signed artifacts, pre/post hash assertions).

Proposal: produce an evidence artifact per meaningful key lifecycle event. Evidence artifact = small JSON blob persisted to evidence-store and included in SIEM export as base64-compact payload/reference. Artifact fields (flat names, used by downstream parsers):
- artifact_id (UUID)
- key_id
- tenant_id
- event_type (rotation_init|rotation_commit|rotation_rollback|escrow_export|hsm_failover)
- event_ts (ISO8601)
- operator (principal id — RBAC subject)
- operator_role (rbac-v2 role name)
- approval_ids (list of approver ids or workflow ids)
- previous_key_fingerprint (sha256 hex)
- new_key_fingerprint (sha256 hex | "null" if rollback)
- hsm_slot (if applicable)
- evidence_sig (hsm_signature | redwood_signing_key)
- operation_result (success|partial|failed)
- audit_log_ref (log stream id / offset)
- attachments (list of artifact refs for archived evidence)

Note: evidence_sig can be an HSM-signed digest where available (private deployments) or Redwood-signature plus escrow metadata for hosted customers. This gives cryptographic binding between the rotation action and the artifact.

SIEM export schema (flattened for ingestion):
- timestamp
- tenant
- event_type
- actor
- actor_role
- artifact_ref (pointer to evidence-store)
- key_id
- prev_fp
- new_fp
- result
- pipeline_tags (array)

We should ensure each SIEM event also includes normalized RBAC context fields: subject_id, subject_type (user/service), session_id, originating_ip, and policy_ids_evaluated.

Section D — Automation patterns and retention

Automation to produce artifacts: rotation workers should generate artifacts as the last step of commit and write to an append-only evidence-store (S3 bucket with object lock versioning) and then publish a compact summary to the SIEM pipeline. Evidence-store objects can be archived to long-term cold tier for legal retention.

Retention guidance (draft):
- Rotation artifacts: 7 years (default for enterprise customers)
- High-fidelity HSM signatures and escrow export logs: 10 years (compliance option)
- Aggregated SIEM summaries: 1 year hot, cold to 7 years

Section E — Example audit log lines (proto)

1) rotation-init (sample flattened log):
{"ts":"2025-01-10T03:12:07Z","tenant":"acme-corp","event":"kms.key.rotate.init","key":"key-0a1b","actor":"svc-kms-rotator","role":"redwood:kms-operator","cohort":"42","artifact_ref":"evidence://a1b2c3"}

2) rotation-commit (with signature):
{"ts":"2025-01-10T03:12:12Z","tenant":"acme-corp","event":"kms.key.rotate.commit","key":"key-0a1b","actor":"approver-ela","role":"security:approver","artifact_ref":"evidence://a1b2c3","evidence_sig":"hsm-sig:MEUCIQ..."}

Section F — Operational checklist (for runbooks)

- Verify cohort-to-key mapping integrity (daily).
- Ensure rotation-worker backlog under threshold (<1000 ops).
- Validate evidence-store write success within 30s of commit.
- SIEM pipeline: ensure mapping of artifact_ref -> object storage is resolvable.
- Weekly sample audit: cryptographically verify evidence_sig for a random 0.5% of rotations.

Open questions and follow-ups (short):
- Decide legal retention defaults per tier (GOV/private vs hosted customers).
- Approver model: human 2-of-3 vs automation+human hybrid — pick one for escrow exports.
- HSM signing availability in Redwood-hosted offering vs Private: plan rollout.
- Performance cost estimation for N=90 cohort plan at scale (need infra input).

Appendix — quick notes and references:
- Related artifacts: CONF-1412, JIRA-SEC-873, KMS-ops PR #291.
- Quick cost model idea: estimate rewrap ops per rotation * HSM op cost + network egress for rewrap under BYOK.
